verified_fact_and_limits: Austin’s council approved a $75 unpaid-meter fine on February 13, 2025, effective March 1. This is the unpaid-meter offense, not every parking violation.

sources.title: Austin council document setting the unpaid-meter fine
sources.qualification: The $75 figure applies to the unpaid-meter fine from March 1, 2025; it is not a universal parking penalty.

verified_fact_and_limits: Des Moines’s 2025 electric-franchise ordinance sets the franchise fee at 7.5%. This is the fee rate, not a claim that every customer’s total bill rose by 7.5%.

sources.title: Des Moines electric-franchise ordinance 16,485
sources.qualification: The ordinance establishes the 7.5% franchise-fee rate. No claim about an individual bill’s total increase or the electric utility’s underlying rates.

verified_fact_and_limits: Sun Metro states that riding the El Paso streetcar is free. This does not establish that every Sun Metro service is fare-free.

sources.title: Sun Metro: About the Streetcars
sources.qualification: Fare-free service applies to the streetcar; no claim about other bus fares, service frequency or reliability.

hook: El Paso’s conditional Meta data-center tax rebate
verified_fact_and_limits: El Paso’s December 2023 agreement offered Meta an 80% city property-tax rebate for the first phase over 15 years, conditional on $800 million investment and 50 jobs. This is not a rebate of all jurisdictions’ taxes or proof the conditions were met.

sources.title: City of El Paso: Data Centers
sources.qualification: First-phase city property-tax rebate: 80%, 15 years, with stated investment and job conditions. No assertion of actual job delivery or exemption from school and county taxes.

hook: Maryland’s public financing for Hagerstown’s stadium
verified_fact_and_limits: Maryland’s 2021 law authorized stadium bonds for Hagerstown. The state announcement also identified $8.5 million in supplemental funding and $1.5 million in fiscal 2023 funding. These figures are not a total project cost or an operating-loss claim.

sources.title: Maryland Stadium Authority: Groundbreaking for the downtown Hagerstown stadium
sources.qualification: Supports the state bond authority and identified public commitments. The resident’s seat exchange is invented; no claim of promised free admission or diversion from a named service.

hook: Iowa City’s extended fare-free bus pilot
verified_fact_and_limits: Iowa City’s December 2025 strategic-plan progress report records an extension of the fare-free transit pilot. An extension is not a permanent fare-free guarantee.

sources.title: Iowa City strategic-plan progress report, December 2025
sources.qualification: Supports extension of the fare-free pilot, not permanent funding or a claim that the program is an actual scientific experiment.

verified_fact_and_limits: Joplin approved sewer-rate adjustments beginning with April 2025 billing, averaging 4% annually from 2025 through 2029. The impact varies by customer; 4% is not every individual bill’s guaranteed increase.

sources.title: Sewer rate adjustment begins for Joplin residents with April 2025 billing
sources.qualification: Average annual change over 2025–2029, with individual impacts varying. No claim about water safety, service failure or an exact household charge.

hook: Wisconsin’s partial veto extending school revenue-limit increases
verified_fact_and_limits: Wisconsin’s Supreme Court upheld Governor Tony Evers’s partial veto that extended school revenue-limit increases to 2425 by deleting characters from the budget text. Revenue limits are not guaranteed future appropriations.

sources.title: AP report on the upheld Wisconsin school revenue-limit veto
sources.qualification: The decision concerns revenue-limit increases through 2425, not an unconditional promise of 400 years of appropriations. The utility-bill comparison is invented satire.

verified_fact_and_limits: Missoula’s current accessory-dwelling-unit code requires no additional parking for an ADU. This does not eliminate all parking rules or other conditions on the proposed dwelling.

sources.title: Missoula municipal code, section 20.45.060: Accessory Dwelling Units
sources.qualification: Uses the current code rather than older planning PDFs. No claim of automatic permit approval or removal of every parking requirement.

verified_fact_and_limits: Rapid City’s council approved vacation-rental regulations in December 2025 that require two off-street parking spaces. The requirement is for covered vacation rentals, not all homes.

sources.title: Rapid City council votes to regulate vacation home rentals
sources.qualification: Supports the two-space requirement under the new vacation-rental rules. No assertion about every existing property’s status or a city requirement that guests use bunk beds.

verified_fact_and_limits: From January 2025, Texas removed most noncommercial vehicle safety inspections and retained a $7.50 inspection-program replacement fee. Applicable emissions inspections and commercial-vehicle inspections remain.

sources.title: Texas DPS: Vehicle Safety Inspection Changes Take Effect January 2025
sources.qualification: Most noncommercial safety inspections ended; applicable emissions and commercial rules remain. The fee is not represented as the entire vehicle-registration bill.

hook: South Dakota’s rejected 2024 consumption-tax ballot measure
verified_fact_and_limits: South Dakota’s official ballot-question history records Initiated Measure 28 failing in 2024, 129,261 to 290,969. The proposal concerned state taxes on goods for human consumption, excluding alcoholic beverages and prepared food; its broader scope was disputed.

sources.title: South Dakota Secretary of State: 2024 Ballot Questions
sources.qualification: Official result: Measure 28 failed, 129,261 to 290,969. The proposal was broader than groceries alone; no claim that it would have eliminated every local tax.

sources.title: South Dakota 2024 General Election Ballot Question Pamphlet
sources.qualification: Attorney General’s explanation describes the state-tax proposal and excludes alcoholic beverages and prepared food. Competing campaign arguments are not treated as established facts.

verified_fact_and_limits: St. Louis’s posted parking-fine schedule lists a $20 meter fine, doubling after 30 days and reaching $80 after 45 days. The schedule is not a universal rule for every parking offense.

sources.title: City of St. Louis: Parking Violation Fines
sources.qualification: Applies to the listed meter violation and payment intervals. No claim that the resident has obtained any investment return or that the rule covers every citation.

verified_fact_and_limits: Oklahoma ended state sales tax on qualifying food and food ingredients on August 29, 2024 under HB 1955. Applicable local sales taxes remain; the exemption does not cover every prepared-food purchase.

sources.title: Oklahoma Tax Commission: State Sales Tax on Food and Food Ingredients
sources.qualification: State exemption for qualifying groceries; local taxes and excluded categories remain. No invented local rate or claim that all food purchases are tax-free.
